Barbie wants to empower women while apparently believing women can’t understand subtext. I’m still trying to figure out who this movie is for. Kids are too young to understand most of what it’s trying to say about womanhood, sexism, beauty standards, motherhood, careers and social expectations. And adult women absolutely do not need a two-hour movie explaining to them that being a woman can be difficult. I’m apparently old enough to understand patriarchy but not old enough to recognize a metaphor without Margot Robbie explaining it to me. It wants to tell women they’re intelligent, strong and capable while simultaneously refusing to trust them to understand a theme unless someone delivers a monologue explaining exactly what it means. That irony might be the most interesting thing in the entire movie.

Je trouve que ça faisait trop mélange entre un long clip musical et une publicité/vitrine géante de « luxe » quasiment. The film is just as plastic and artificial as the source material it’s based on. I was severely disappointed after I finished the film. It has no nuance, no depth and for me, it’s just a vapid, virtue signaling mess. The problem isn’t the moral core of the film, which I do agree with, but how it’s dealt with. In my opinion it feels surface level and strangely disingenuous. This isn’t helped by the story, which has no twists and no particularly strong plot, it’s just filled with a bunch of underdeveloped characters that flash their fake smile at you as they wave the films message in your face like a great pink neon sign. That being said, the film has its moments, but most of these come from the more silly joke driven bits and are quickly overshadowed by the “I’m fourteen and this is deep” level existentialism. It’s like Gerwig was torn between making a film for young girls and a serious feminist film, and then from that inner battle rose this compromise, which fails to deliver on either. Still, thanks for all the silly goofs it’s not unbearable watch, at times it’s almost entertaining. Though, it’s a crime that the song Barbie Girl was not once played. Shame.

Un film qui m’a plutôt surpris par ce qu’il cherche à raconter derrière son apparence de comédie colorée et légère. Barbie est évidemment très drôle et possède une identité visuelle vraiment réussie. Les décors, les costumes et la direction artistique donnent au film une personnalité qu’on reconnaît immédiatement. Margot Robbie et Ryan Gosling sont également excellents, avec un Ryan Gosling qui vole presque la vedette à chacune de ses apparitions. J’ai surtout apprécié le fait que le film ne se contente pas de faire une simple adaptation de la poupée Barbie. Il aborde des sujets plus sérieux sur les attentes liées aux hommes et aux femmes, l’identité et la place qu’on cherche à trouver dans la société. Cependant, malgré toutes ses qualités, je n’ai pas été aussi touché que je l’aurais voulu. Certains messages sont parfois un peu trop appuyés et le film m’a semblé perdre un peu de son charme lorsqu’il devient plus sérieux. Une comédie originale, drôle et très bien réalisée, avec de bonnes idées et d’excellentes performances, mais qui ne m’aura pas totalement convaincu.

Greta Gerwig left subtlety and her serious face at the door for this one, and in the hands of a less capable cast and crew, it would probably fall apart. But what makes Barbie work is the absurdity and the cast and crew not taking things seriously. Ultimately, the issues it tackles are ridiculous one that really shouldn’t be issues anyway (equality, acceptance, etc.) and so making a movie that doesn’t take itself seriously and pokes fun at everything is the perfect way to tackle such absurdity. I think some people fell into the trap of trying to look below the surface of this movie, but with Barbie , what you see is what you get, and that is not at all a bad thing. I did have a couple issues with certain characters feeling a bit too flat and I thought the real world stuff was kinda boring, but overall I think this movie works really well and accomplishes all that it set out to do. Greta Gerwig is a really fantastic director and I very much look forward to her take on Narnia.

I think Barbie is one of those movies I wish every little girl could watch before the world gets the chance to tell her who she is supposed to be. Because underneath all the pink and glitter, it is a story about becoming a woman. About growing up and slowly realizing that there is no version of yourself that will ever be enough for everyone. Be beautiful, but not vain. Be smart, but not intimidating. Be strong, but still soft. Have ambition, but don't make anyone feel small. Be independent, but still be desirable. How exhausting it is to be a woman and constantly feel like you're failing at a set of rules that were never meant to be followed. And then Barbie asks you to let all of that go. To exist without having to be perfect. To be messy, uncertain, angry, joyful, ordinary. To grow older without believing you've become less valuable. To understand that your worth was never supposed to depend on how well you fit into someone else's idea of a woman. Maybe that's why this movie means so much to me. I wish little girls could see it before they learn to shrink themselves. Before they learn to apologize for taking up space. Before they learn that being loved sometimes means becoming smaller. I want them to grow up knowing that they don't have to be the prettiest, the smartest, the kindest, or the most accomplished person in the room. They just have to know that their life belongs to them. And maybe that's what Barbie really changed for me: Being a woman isn't about becoming the perfect version of yourself. It's about finally realizing you were never meant to be a version of anyone else.

J’ai beaucoup aimé les moments où Lizzo chantait et conversait avec Barbie pendant la chanson. Par contre le Real World est moche, mais vraiment. Tout est gris, je peux comprendre la logique de faire une transition radicale entre le monde coloré des Barbie et le vrai monde mais on passe juste d’un monde magnifique à un monde morne et gris. Le film ne prend pas le temps de bien développer ses personnages et le rythme du récit est trop rapide, on ne s’attarde pas plus de quelques minutes sur une scène. Ce qui fait qu’il est difficile de s’attacher aux personnages, surtout Barbie parce qu’elle a un arc émotionnel intéressant. L’arc de Will Ferrell et de Mattel est très oubliable et pas forcément nécessaire au film. Le plot d’America Ferrara et sa fille : quel gros ronpiche, je n’en avais rien à cirer du début à la fin. Seule sa tirade finale sur la dissonance cognitive sur ce qu’est être une femme dans notre société est mémorable. Certains sujets sont traités un peu maladroitement mais ça n’était pas trop un problème pour moi. C’est justement ce que j’attendais le plus de Greta Gerwig, une des mes valeurs sûres : un bon traitement émotionnel. Je peux dire que celui qu’on a eu est très brouillon et ne marche pas toujours. On ne fait pas dans la finesse, on frôle même la grossièreté sur quelques passages. Certaines blagues sont remplies de buzz-words et faites pour cibler la Gen-Z ce qui donne un air faux mais ça ne concerne encore une fois que quelques répliques donc ça va. Margot Robbie est Margot Robbie, sans trop de surprises, elle est talentueuse mais rien de particulier ici. Par contre, Ryan Gosling se dépasse, il est vraiment amusant et ridicule, ça cimente sa réputation d’acteur comique pour moi. C’est lui qui a le plus retenu mon attention. D’autant plus que je ne l’avais jamais entendu chanter comme ça, pas même dans La La Land (2016), il pousse bien la chansonnette ! Sa séquence de transformation en comédie musicale à la fin est remarquable ! J’ai passé un bon moment, j’ai ri, les références sont intelligentes, des blagues justes et certains passages sont bien pensés. Je pense aussi qu’ils ont dévoilés trop de passages du film, pas les plus importants pour l’intrigue mais des blagues majeures qui font plus le même effet une fois qu’on les entendues une première fois. Pour résumer, c’est un film divertissant que j’ai pris du plaisir à regarder mais avec quelques défauts non négligeables qui ont un peu limé mon appréciation.

One thing that always brings a smile to my face is the memories of our children playing in our home. To have three daughters who all had long blond hair and the natural beauty of their mother, it came to be a natural consideration that they would receive Barbie dolls as gifts. Our girls had a pink carry case filled with these dolls, clothing, and accessories. We didn’t overthink what message this sent to them as they travelled into their teen years, where body image would become a significant issue. Ultimately, these dolls provided hours of joy for our girls, and to think I would be talking about these toys as adults hadn't occurred to me. Except the world has been taken over by a pink wave of Barbie-mania with the upcoming release of the live-action film starring Margot Robbie (Babylon) and Ryan Gosling (La La Land) as Barbie and Ken, respectively. Granted, it makes you wonder how two Academy Award-nominated actors could be involved in the Mattel-sponsored film project. That is until you see that the filmmakers are the exceptionally talented wife/husband team, Greta Gerwig (Little Women), and Noah Baumbach (Marriage Story). This surprising choice to helm this film has led to much speculation about the satirical messaging and artistic style of Barbie’s journey into self-awareness and purpose. Unlike the animated films that have defined this blond icon to generations, Gerwig’s adaptation has the central character living in the idyllic world of Barbieland. A world where everything seemingly is perfect with there being a balance of cultural representation and the ‘Barbies’ rule the community. The Kens of the community primarily serve as eye candy and try to impress the Barbies of this land. Until the central Barbie (Robbie) begins to have thoughts connected to the real world, such as death and cellulite. After a counselling session with weird Barbie (Kate McKinnon), Barbie decides to travel by toy-generated montage to the real world to find her true owner, and she is unexpectedly joined by Ken (Gosling). Yet, upon arrival, she realises that the real world is not the utopia she had expected when she left her life behind. Let's get it out of the way, I'm not the target audience for this film. I will admit this up front, but I do appreciate good entertainment regardless of the package it might be delivered in. Despite the indulgent use of pink, the over-the-top antics of the cast, and the obviously satirical nature of the humour, I did my best to enjoy this movie. Alas, I failed to find much that I enjoyed about this Barbie adventure. At first, it was difficult to put a finger on what it was about this story that didn’t sit right with me, since the initial tone of the film was manufactured joy that comes from movies about toys. Yet, nothing seemed quite right within this plasticine world despite the yearning to honour the fond memories of my daughters' youth. Also, throughout the years, I have appreciated the artistry of Greta Gerwig and Noah Baumbach, even though much of their work tends toward a darker and biting depiction of the human condition. Then it hit me that amongst this tale of fabricated dreams, the filmmakers are trying to redefine the image of the iconic doll from a poor example of body image and femininity into a potential poster child for feminism. Yet, as they attempt to dismantle the vicious nature of this world's definition of toxic masculinity and women’s self-identity, they managed to create an atmosphere of toxic femininity. Instead of offering an alternative to many of the world’s issues with gender division, they chose to replace the problems by mirroring the points on the opposite end of the sexual identity scale. They could have provided a balanced, heart-warming world where Barbies and Kens could exist in equilibrium and harmony. Yet, all they do is replace one form of oppression with another. As they unpack this messaging, something that does stand out in this screenplay is the message that men and women are different. Gerwig and Baumbach show that there is no middle ground between the sexes and despite their sardonic view of these worlds, they show that there are only two genders. Not even the Alan (Michael Cera) character can admit to being anything other than male. In this current media climate, it is fascinating to see this portrayal within the discussion of sexual politics. This might be one of the few things that I agree with about this film, but this gets me to the real challenge with this movie. Barbie (The Movie) is not for children. Unlike The Lego Movie’s mocking manner that appeals to adults and little ones, Barbie is meant for adults only. Yes, it does have a PG rating, but the filmmakers push this system to the limit with innuendo and clever wordsmithing. Despite being an unapologetic advertisement for the doll and the world that she represents, Mattel has greenlit a story that is only meant for the women who played with the dolls as children. Initially, this film feels like it is designed for all, but eventually proves to be a divisive and unappealing view of Barbieloand and reality that isn’t intended for the target market of the doll. For the sake of my family, I truly wanted to give this film the love that comes from a lifetime of adoring memories. Still, in the end, Barbie offers very little for little girls or their parents to enjoy. Reel Dialogue: The value of mothers There are many topics we could hash out about Barbie in this section, but the one I would like to highlight is the value of mothers. The most endearing character in the film is Gloria (America Ferrera), a Mattel employee struggling to connect with her teenage daughter. Her speech about the plight of women in the real world is one of the best parts of this screenplay. Within it, she unpacks the value of women, how they are uniquely created, and that each has value in the roles at home and at work. As she redefines her relationship with her daughter, this working mother shows her importance as a mentor, example, and, most notably, as a mom. In this world that places more importance on the woman outside of the home, this glimmer of hope within the overwhelming pink display shows how women are needed in their children's lives. Not that every woman in this world will have offspring of their own, but they can know that they do have an essential role in the investment of future generations. As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you; you shall be comforted in Jerusalem. - Isaiah 66:13 God created and designed mothers to be a beautiful representation of His love for the world. This shows the importance and value of this role to humanity, and these women must be celebrated. Take some time today and show your mother how much you appreciate her today.

Stellt euch den grandiosen LEGO Movie vor und ersetzt alle durch den Cast von Sex Education in einem viel zu lang gezogenen SNL-Sketch. Man spürt die Spielfreude. Die Meta-Jokes sind oft brillant. Vieles davon wird sich jetzt für immer in unsere Popkultur brennen. Nur alles dazwischen ist die gender-geswapte Version von Tom Gerhardt auf dem Ballermann. Und so präzise und so witzig die sozialkritischen Beobachtungen sind, so haarsträubend sind die Schlussfolgerungen daraus: Ein Geschlecht unterdrückt das andere Geschlecht. Also tyrannisiert dieses Geschlecht dann wiederum das andere - nur um als Lösung doch wieder ein Geschlecht das andere unterdrücken zu lassen. Als Lösung! Jetzt ist alles wieder gut. Wenn man wirklich darüber nachdenkt, ist das ist in der Konsequenz einer der toxischsten Filme des Jahres. Und wären die Geschlechter vertauscht, würden wir jetzt alle auf die Straße gehen. Aber hey, es ist ja nur Barbie , oder? ------------- Und weil das alles völlig falsch mansplained von dem LEGO-spielenden Typen ist, hier ein paar nachträgliche Ergänzungen nach der Eskalation in den Kommentaren: - Ich sage, dass die sozialkritischen Beobachtungen richtig und wichtig sind. Ich finde sie richtig und wichtig, weil wir alle die Benachteiligungen von Frauen sehen. - Ich interpretiere nur die Aussage am Ende als kontraproduktiv. Das ist meine Interpretation der Aussage. Das kann jeder anders sehen oder als nicht so gewichtig erachten. Für mich hinterlässt das nunmal einen faden Beigeschmack. - Das ist nicht der alleinige Grund für die 2 Sterne. Ich sage ja, dass ich mit dem restlichen Humor abseits der Meta-Jokes wirklich gar nichts anfangen kann. Und das ist bei 2 1/2 Stunden länge halt nicht meins. - Das ist eine Meinung. Die kann man richtig scheiße finden. Vielleicht sogar toxisch. Aber dass die Antworten darauf dann Todeswünsche und Entmenschlichung in jeder Art und Weise sind, ist nicht der Spiegel, den mir einige vielleicht vorhalten wollen, sondern nur selbstentlarvend. Und wie ich in dieser Review versuche auszudrücken: Unrecht mit Unrecht auszugleichen, bringt niemanden weiter.

Bu film çıkmadan önce film hakkında o kadar sert düşüncelere sahiptim ki kendi kendime “sanırım ben bu filmi asla beğenmeyeceğim” tarzı düşüncelere kapılmıştım. Çünkü filmin tanıtım süreci en azından bence o kadar kötü yapıldı ki filmin ciddiyetini ortadan bir anda kaldırdı ve çok gereksiz büyük bir beklenti oluşturdu. Hatta filmin fragmanları bizlere filmin aşırı ciddiyetsiz bir Barbie filmi izleyeceğimizin sinyallerini adeta bağırarak veriyordu ve ben de bundan dolayı filmle alakalı pek olumlu fikirlere sahip değildim. Ancak filmi izledikten sonra kendi kendime yarattığım bu ciddiyeti kırmam gerektiğinin farkına vardım ve filmi daha güzel değerlendirebildim. Barbie, bir Barbie filmi nasıl olması gerekiyorsa o havayı sizlere gayet iyi veren, eğlenceli, komik ve düşündüren bir yapım olmuş. Özellikle filmin 2. Yarısı anlatı yönünden epey güçlü ve hayatını Barbie oyuncakları ile geçirmiş insanlar için oldukça kıymetli sahnelere sahip. Bu açıdan filmi her ne kadar beklediğim derecede kötü bulmasam da çok gözüme batan birkaç gereksiz sahnesi ve yer yer kendi beceriksizliğinden doğan ton tutarsızlıkları nedeniyle filme çok bayılmadım. Ki zaten film başta çok tuhaf bir ton ile açılıyor ve ilk yarım saatinde olayları çok plastik bir hale sokuyor. Bu da doğal olarak sizi filmde yaşananları hiçbir şekilde ciddiye almamanız gereken bir psikolojiye sürüklüyor ama film 2.yarısında olaylarını öyle bir noktaya getiriyor ki Barbie’nin temsil ettiği bir takım klişe şeyler filmin çok ciddi birer teması haline gelmeye başlıyor. Özellikle Barbie’nin popüler kültüre ve insanlara kattığı şeylerin farkına vardığı sahneler filmin en vurucu anları ve film buralarda anlatı olarak çok sağlam bir temele sahip. Daha da üstüne günümüzün çok klişe sayılan bir takım bakış açılarıyla film çok güzel bir dil ile dalga geçiyor ve seyircisini epey eğlendiriyor. Bu yerlerde de film hem kendi seviyesini hem de espri anlayışını çok iyi bir noktaya taşıyor ve hayranlarını en azından bence çok memnun etmeyi başarıyor. Ayrıca Margot Robbie ve Ryan Gosling rollerine öyle yakışmışlar ki izlerken epey hoşuma gitti ve beni epey eğlendirdi. Özellikle Ryan Gosling Ken rölünü o kadar benimsemişki kendi başına filmin bazı noktalarını çok güzel sırtlamış. Aynı cümleleri Margot Robbie için de söylemek oldukça mümkün. Özellikle filmin kendisiyle ilgili dalga geçtiği kısımlar filmde epey eğlenceliydi. Zaten filmin genel oyunculuk performansları ve tercihleri epey başarılı. Herkes üstüne düşüne fazla fazla yerine getirmiş. Ancak filmin ilk yarısı çok sinir bozucu bir takım kararlara sahip olduğu için film tam potansiyeline ne yazık ki benim gözümde ulaşamıyor. Özellikle açılış sahnesinin tonu o kadar sinir bozucu ki öykündüğü filmin hayranı olan ben bu sahneye epey sinir oldum. Çünkü film esinlendiği eserin hem bütün ciddiyetini bozuyor hem de onun sayesinde kendine çok güzel bir temele sahip bir sahne katıyor. Yani filmin çok ikon olmuş olan açılış sahnesi bildiğiniz çalıyor ama esinlendiği eserin ciddiyeti kadar ciddi bir ton sunmadığı için bu kullanım çok yalan olmaya başlıyor. Spirited, inherently hopeless effort to reconcile all the competing imperatives of making a live-action Barbie movie in the year 2023. It's knowing prefab camp that both revels in and loudly interrogates the retro appeal of Barbie. It's representationally inclusive while gently acknowledging that Mattel's forays into diversifying Barbie were, of course, financially motivated. It bites the hand that feeds (plays?) by pointing out the gender disparity within a company with a predominately female consumer base, while also covering for that company by making it look hip and self-aware enough to cop to its disparities. It nods to everything bad that's ever been said or written about Barbie as an iconic product even as it essentially gives everyone permission to forget all that and have fun. (Apropos the Kubrick reference of the opening scene, its subtitle could be How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bombshell .) It's practically the textbook definition of corporate feminism, but it knows that too, of course, and is earnest in using the platform of a big-budget toy commercial to speak to the audience about the patriarchy; there's a big speech that recalls the one Laura Dern delivers in Marriage Story , which makes me wonder if Baumbach counterintuitively wrote this one or if Gerwig helped him write that one. Even its lionization of the woman behind Barbie comes with an asterisk. The whole thing is animated by neurosis more than joy, which is what I found most interesting about it: Is there a little of Gerwig's offscreen wrestling with the assignment in Barbie's onscreen existential crisis? Wish it was a little funnier.

Gün saydığımız Barbenheimer seferinin ilk yarısını bu sabah tamamladım. Alışılagelen eleştirel söylevimden bir nebze saparak film hakkındaki düşüncelerimi; olumlu & olumsuz kısımlarını maddeler halinde sayarak, anlayacağınız direkt artı/eksi tablosuyla ele alayım dedim. Öyleyse pozitif başlayalım. + İçinde envai çeşit Barbie, Ken (ve bir adet Allen)’ı barındıran Barbieland dudak uçuklatan bir prodüksiyon dizaynına sahip. Barbie’lerin evlerindeki minik detaylara bayıldım; setler, hayali bir Barbie dünyası yerine gerçektende çocukların evlerindeki oyuncaklara benzetilmiş. Bu nedenle buzdolabındaki materyaller basit bir çıkartmadan, havuz ise yer kaplamasından ibaret. Arabalarda motor bile yok. Karakterler yemek/ içecekleri gerçekten mideye indirmektense tüketiyormuş gibi yapıyorlar. Bu hayali dünyanın fizik kuralları her ne kadar gerçeküstü olsa da; mekanlardaki her ayrıntı, yalnızca gerçek bir Barbie oyuncağında bulacağınız unsurlarla dolu. Kostüm tasarımında da muazzam bir iş çıkarılmış. Her Barbie’nin, zamanında satışa çıkan gerçek bir oyuncağın kıyafetini giymesi ve elbiselerin sahneler boyunca sürekli değişiklik göstermesi takdir edilesi bir çalışma olmuş. Aktörlerin kusursuz saçından bahsetmiyorum bile. Şüphesiz ödül sezonunda bu dallardan en az birisinde rakiplerini yerle bir edecektir. - Vizyona adım atmadan öncesinde seyirciye merak aşılayan aktörler; filmin basit bir oyuncak bebeğin hikayesinden ziyade çok daha derin anlamlar içerdiğinden, yaşam & ölüm konseptini felsefik bir perspektifle incelediğinden bahsetmişlerdi. Hatta Ryan Gosling, Barbie ’nin kariyerinde okuduğu en iyi senaryo olduğunu dahi belirtmişti. Yani, o kadar da uçmaya gerek yokmuş. Barbie her ne kadar mevzubahis konulara parmak bassa da, temasını belirtme şekli hem silik hem de oldukça bariz. Biraz daha açmak gerekirse; film, varoluş krizine değinerek bizlere ölümü hatırlatırken sonrasında ise küçük bir kızın mutsuzluğuna zıplayarak insaoğlunun kapitalist çıkarları gereği kendini mahvetmesine ışık tutuyor. Hemen ardından kadın olmanın ne demek olduğuna ve bu etiketin getirdiği mazur görülemez beklentilere değinerek kadınların çektiği zorluklara parmak basılıyor. En sondaysa kadınlardan da öte, insan olmanın ne olduğu sorgulanıp bir kişiyi tanımlayan olgunun ne olduğu araştırılıyor. Anlayacağınız bukalemun gibi perde başına tema değiştirmekte; ilk önce yaşamak , sonra kadın olmak , en son ise insan olmak irdeleniyor. Yalnızca bununla da kalmayıp odaklandığı mevzuları da kör göze parmak bir şekilde işlemekte. Örneğin kadın olmanın zorlukları; dünyamızdaki toplumların davranış biçimlerinden değil, doğrudan bir insan tarafından bu zorlukların haykırılmasıyla dile getirilmekte. Üçüncü perdedeki Ruth sekansı (spoiler vermeden), her ne kadar duygusal ve manâlı bir an doğursa da, aynı zamanda o esnada verilen mesajlar fazlasıyla göze sokuluyordu. + Fragmanlarda gösterildiği için rahatça bahsetmek gerekirse, Ken’in dünyaya geldikten sonra ataerkilliği keşfettiği sahneler ağız dolusu kahkahalar attıracak noktalarla doluydu. Feminen bir dünyada geçirdiği onca zamandan sonra bizim dünyamızdaki erkeklerin dominasyonunu ve masküleniteyi öğrendiği anlar, belki de filmin en komik parçalarından birisi olabilir. Drama janrasında bolca kol gezen Ryan Gosling, umarım bu yapımdan sonra daha fazla komedide yer almaya başlar. Fazlasıyla satirize edilmiş karakterine kazandırdığı kişilik, paha biçilemezdi. Meme lorduna dönen Beyciğimin sunduğu performans sayesinde, internet birkaç ay daha meme lerin ekmeğini yer herhalde. - İki saatlik süresine rağmen ikinci perdeden itibaren birçok kez esnediğim ve gözümü ovaladığım anlar oldu. Bir noktadan sonra tempo yönetiminde topallamaya başlayan Barbie , ikinci yarısında fazlasıyla kestirilebilir bir kapanışı takip ediyor. İlk yarıya doğru ilerlerken Barbie ile Ken’in yollarının ayrıldığı bir sahneye şahit oluyoruz, bu sahneden itibaren filmin geri kalanı, en azından benim gözümde oldukça barizdi. Bu noktadan sonra tek yapmam gereken şey, tahmin ettiğim olayların yaşanmasını beklemekti. Sürpriz faktörünü yitirmesinden ötürü son perde sakız gibi uzamaya başladı. Nihayetinde film, beni bitişe doğru oldukça yormayı başardı. + Barbie ’nin iki sinefil tarafından yazıldığı, sahneler boyunca durmaksızın maruz kaldığımız film göndermeleriyle rahatlıkla anlaşılıyor. İlk önce 2001: A Space Odyssey , ardından The Godfather , sonrasında The Matrix … derken bir anda Zack Snyder’s Justice League ! Filmin sinemaya duyduğu saygıya şapka çıkartıyorum. - Film başlamadan önce Mattel bu fırsatı kaçırmayarak yapımdan bağımsız reklamlar sıkıştırmış araya. TLC’nin Barbie programından tutun oyuncağın apaçık tanıtımına kadar onca anlamsız reklam izledik. Filmle pek alakası olmayabilir ama bu durum, beni uyuz etmedi desem yalan olur. + Salondan çıktıktan sonra hemen Spotify listesine saldırmasam da, müzikler fena değildi. Dua Lipa ve Billie Eilish’in parçalarını gayet beğendim, sahnelerle oldukça uyumlu ve duyusal tesiri arttıracak niteliğe sahip. Nicki Minaj’ın parçası ise… eh işte, Anaconda ablam yine kendi kulvarında yapmış bir şeyler. Peki film sinemada izlenmeli mi? Bu soruyu cevaplamak inanın bir hayli zor. Çünkü okuduğum eleştirilere göre azınlıkta görünüyorum. Bu nedenle direkt “Gitmeyin!” demek, izlediği takdirde beğenecek arkadaşlara haksızlık olur. Sadece bilin ki, bu film bahsedildiği kadar derin anlam içeren veya bir yetişkinin zihnini gıdıklayacak unsurlara yer vermiyor. Hatta bütününe bakacak olursak, çocuk filmi olduğu gerçeği daha ağır basıyor. Filmi bu Cuma bir daha izleyeceğim; eğer puanım 6/10’un üzerine çıkarsa, bilin ki filme olan bakış açım bir nebze değişmiş ve Barbie ’ye daha çok ısınmışımdır. Şu anda Barbenheimer yarışmasında ikinciliği elde tutuyor, hangi rakibin galibiyeti elinde tutacağını hem yarın Oppenheimer izlediğimde hem de Cuma iki filmi de tekrardan izlediğimde belli olacak. if you’re familiar with gerwig’s filmography, then you know the themes that take up space inside of her and shine through all of her work, and you’ll find them here as well. the meditation on what Barbie is directed by Greta Gerwig and stars Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling as the main leads. I am so excited to give you this review early, so here is my thoughts on the highly anticipated movie Barbie. I’ve been a fan of Gerwig’s work since Lady Bird which is an absolute one of the best coming to age films in the last couple of years and Little Woman is definitely one of the better literature work in the last decade. This is Gerwig’s first time directing a full on pop culture property on a toy franchise that has been going on for 70 + years. Going in for this movie I was extremely excited and had really high expectations, after the movie finished I have confidence that Greta Gerwig is a 3 for 3 director and proves to be one of the strongest  young female voices in Hollywood today. Margot Robbie gives one of her best performances as Barbie and her character study is absolutely needed for female characters in films today. Early Test Screenings for this film has been praising Ryan Gosling Ken’s Performance calling it the best performances yet and I absolutely agree. Ryan Gosling as Ken is gonna be memed heavily and will recieved a cult following of his performance and hopefully snag a nomination for supporting actor because he’s incredible and stole the show and of course his performance is based on me. Other performances in this film including America Ferrera as Gloria is very good and there is an important scene in this film in which she delivers on her performance. Other performances like Emma Mackey, Simu Liu, Hari Nef, Kate McKinnon, Issae Rae, Dua Lipa and all of the performances in the film gives their characters a lot of personality and Will Ferrell’s best performance in almost a decade. The Costumes and Production Design captures the imagination as if you were playing a Barbie doll with a doll house and with Rodrigo Prieto cinematography makes this one of the most colorful and vibrant colors inspired by 1960s fashion and films that is heavily inspired by the projects from Jacques Demy from the French New Wave and of course The Wizard of Oz. The 2nd half of the film I absolutely loved and the way how Gerwig and Baumbach’s amazing screenplay gives a lot of risks on its ambitions that I think it’s not really for everyone so it will be mixed on but I absolutely think it contains one of the best scenes for a comedy film in a very long time with a 3rd act that has a lot of emotions yet contains one of the best sequences of the year. Gerwig’s complete reimagining of Barbie gives what we love about the late 90s and early 2000 comfort chick flicks but also delivers a serious deep message that will definitely not leave the audiences mind when the film is over. Barbie is one of the best movies of the year and probably the best feel good comedy in a very long time. Please support Barbenheimer and Oppenheimer when it hits theaters July 21st.
